notes: Effective policy until the Product Owner decides: keep the latest listing of apps the user tracks (no history), show the App Store link with every app, no icons or screenshots, no export.

Apple: promotional content (previews, artwork, app icons) may be used 'only to promote store content and not for entertainment purposes'. App Spy therefore does not display or store icons or screenshots.
Apple's Search API pages say nothing about storing listing metadata; absence of a rule is not a permission.
The developer website is fetched once, only when the user asks, only the URL the store lists, with the SSRF guard (public addresses, http/https, 1 MB, 10 s, 3 redirects).

conditions: Daily rating/version snapshots for tracked apps only, kept 365 days.
Exports for internal research only, each row with its App Store URL.
No icons, screenshots or previews stored or exported.

notes: Documented: 'approximately 20 calls per minute (subject to change)'; heavier use should go through the Enterprise Partner Feed.
The client paces itself to one call every 3.1 s per process; APPLE_SEARCH_DAILY_REQUESTS caps a day (default 2000).
Observed in 2 PoC runs (2026-11-27 01:19 and 01:27 UTC+7): 18/18 HTTP 200, no 403/429; p50 about 300 ms.

limitations: Search is fuzzy: a nonsense term still returned 3 loosely related apps (A3). Treat search results as suggestions; track by id.
Up to 200 results per search; no pagination and no sort by popularity, rank or downloads.
No download counts, revenue, keyword rank or chart position. App Spy never estimates them.
Ratings, prices and availability are per storefront (country).
Lookup by bundle id works but is not documented (PARTIAL).
sellerUrl (developer website) is listed for about 71–75% of apps in the PoC sample; the rest cannot be linked.
No reviews endpoint in this API (the RSS customer-review feed is not part of it and is not used).
